title: Real-World Effectiveness of High-Dose Tafamidis on Neurologic Disease Progression in Mixed-Phenotype Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy
off: Real-World Effectiveness of High-Dose Tafamidis on Neurologic Disease Progression in Mixed-Phenotype Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM)
summary: This study will examine the clinical effectiveness of Tafamidis in patients with Mixed Phenotype Transthyretin Amyloidosis using data that already exist in patients' medical records
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age ≥18 years at diagnosis.
* Diagnosed with ATTRv-CM or ATTRwt-CM, mixed phenotype.
* Treated with tafamidis, as VYNDAMAX 61 mg (one 61-mg tafamidis capsule) orally once daily for ≥12 months or started on tafamidis 20 mg then switched to VYNDAMAX 61 mg for ≥12 months
* Have had ≥1 pre- and ≥1 post-treatment neurologic assessments.

Exclusion Criteria:

* History of any organ transplant.
* Individuals who are non-ambulatory.
* Prior or current treatment with any disease-modifying therapy (investigational or approved) alone or in combination, except tafamidis, as VYNDAQEL 80 mg \[four 20-mg tafamidis meglumine capsules\] orally once daily or VYNDAMAX 61 mg \[one 61-mg tafamidis capsule\] orally once daily.
* Peripheral neuropathy attributed to causes other than ATTR amyloidosis (eg, diabetes mellitus, B12 deficiency, hypothyroidism, shingles,Lyme disease, HIV infection, secondary to injury, chronic kidney disease).
* Patient's data fails to pass data quality checks.

arms.d: ATTR-CM patients presenting with mixed phenotype

primary.tf: Baseline through at least 12 months of treatment

pubs.cit: Fine NM, Streicher NS, Conceição I, Agostinho J, Obici L, Palladini G, et al. Neurologic Stability During Tafamidis Treatment in Transthyretin Amyloidosis with a Mixed Phenotype: A Multicenter Real-World Study. Cardiol Ther. 2026. doi: 10.1007/s40119-026-00479-z

abstracts:
Fine NM, Streicher NS, Conceição I, Agostinho J, Obici L, Palladini G, et al. Neurologic Stability During Tafamidis Treatment in Transthyretin Amyloidosis with a Mixed Phenotype: A Multicenter Real-World Study. Cardiol Ther. 2026. doi: 10.1007/s40119-026-00479-z
INTRODUCTION: Real-world evidence on the effect of tafamidis in mixed-phenotype transthyretin (TTR) amyloidosis (ATTR amyloidosis) is limited. This study assessed changes in neurologic and other measures in patients with mixed-phenotype ATTR amyloidosis treated with tafamidis free acid 61 mg for ≥ 12 months in routine clinical practice.
METHODS: This observational, non-interventional, retrospective multicenter cohort study used anonymized data from four centers. Adults with variant or wild-type mixed-phenotype ATTR amyloidosis treated with tafamidis 61 mg for ≥ 12 months with pre- and post-treatment neurologic assessments were eligible. The primary objective was to assess changes in neurologic measures after ≥ 12 months of treatment; secondary and exploratory objectives were to assess changes in cardiac and frailty measures, modified body mass index (mBMI), and TTR concentration.
RESULTS: Overall, 67 patients were included (median age 77.0 years; 79.1% male patients; 55.2% with variant ATTR amyloidosis). Median duration of treatment with tafamidis 61 mg was 35.0 months. Neuropathy Impairment Score (NIS) motor subscale, NIS reflex subscale, and Medical Research Council Scale for Muscle Strength scores showed a median change of 0 from baseline after ≥ 12 months of treatment. Cardiac measures demonstrated minimal change, although interventricular septal thickness (median change, 0.1 cm; p = 0.017) and left atrial diameter (median change, 0.3 cm; p = 0.018) increased modestly. Median change in mBMI was 6.7 g/L × kg/m2 (p = 0.925), and 90% of patients with data remained within the same Essential Frailty Toolset score range. TTR concentration increased significantly (median change, 3.0 mg/dL; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world study of patients with variant or wild-type mixed-phenotype ATTR amyloidosis, neurologic, cardiac, mBMI, and frailty measures were largely maintained after ≥ 12 months of treatment with tafamidis 61 mg. TTR concentration significantly increased. These findings provide real-world evidence of maintenance of neurologic function during treatment with tafamidis in mixed-phenotype ATTR amyloidosis.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06393465.

x.titre: Tafamidis 61 mg en vie réelle : progression neurologique dans l'amylose ATTR cardiaque à phénotype mixte
x.question: Le tafamidis ralentit-il la progression de l'atteinte neurologique chez des patients ayant une amylose ATTR cardiaque à phénotype mixte (cardiaque et neurologique) ?
x.contexte:
L'amylose à transthyrétine (ATTR) peut toucher le cœur (cardiomyopathie, ATTR-CM) et les nerfs périphériques (polyneuropathie). Dans les formes à phénotype mixte, l'atteinte cardiaque et l'atteinte neurologique coexistent, que la maladie soit héréditaire (ATTRv) ou sauvage (ATTRwt).

Le tafamidis est un stabilisateur de la transthyrétine. Dans l'essai ATTR-ACT, il a réduit la mortalité toutes causes et les hospitalisations cardiovasculaires dans la cardiomyopathie ; il a aussi été étudié à plus faible dose dans la polyneuropathie ATTRv débutante. Son effet sur l'évolution neurologique des patients à phénotype mixte, traités à la dose cardiologique de 61 mg (Vyndamax), est mal documenté.

Cette étude observationnelle rétrospective, promue par Pfizer, utilise des données de dossiers médicaux d'un centre unique. Elle compare l'évolution des évaluations neurologiques avant et après au moins 12 mois de tafamidis 61 mg. Elle ne comporte pas de groupe contrôle sans traitement.
x.interet: Elle pourrait documenter, en pratique courante, un effet du tafamidis à dose cardiologique sur la composante neurologique. L'absence de bras témoin et le caractère rétrospectif limitent toutefois la portée des conclusions.
x.profil: Des adultes ayant une amylose ATTR cardiaque à phénotype mixte, traités par tafamidis 61 mg depuis au moins 12 mois.
inclusion: Tafamidis 61 mg (Vyndamax) une fois par jour depuis ≥ 12 mois, ou 20 mg puis 61 mg ≥ 12 mois
Au moins une évaluation neurologique avant et une après traitement
exclusion: Autre traitement modificateur de la maladie, en dehors du tafamidis 80 mg ou 61 mg
Neuropathie périphérique d'une autre cause (diabète, carence en B12, hypothyroïdie, zona, Lyme, VIH, insuffisance rénale chronique…)
Données ne passant pas le contrôle qualité

bras.traitement: Tafamidis 61 mg par voie orale, une fois par jour, depuis au moins 12 mois

x.duree: Données rétrospectives : au moins 12 mois de traitement ; aucune visite dédiée
x.critere: Taux de progression de l'atteinte neurologique entre l'inclusion et au moins 12 mois de traitement.
